predecessors.note: Ratimir's Slavic realm around the Drava and Sava, deposed in 838; Cliopatria's Avar Khaganate ended in 805 and no state with a dossier held the land between.

successors.note: 'Frankish domination ... lasted until the Magyar conquest (c. 900)'; after the Battle of Pressburg (907) 'no further Slavic rulers are recorded' in Lower Pannonia.

capitals.name: Mosapurc / Blatnohrad (Zalavár)
capitals.note: Pribina 'began to build in 846 a large fortress as his seat of power' near Zalavár; for 838-845 the pages name no seat, so the same site is carried back (bridge).

rulers.name: Pribina
rulers.note: Installed by the Franks in 838 (Principality of Lower Pannonia page); the formal grant of the Zala region is dated 10 January 846 (Pribina page); died 861, either fighting Moravians or captured and handed to them.

rulers.name: Kocel
rulers.title: Comes de Sclauis
rulers.note: Succeeded in 861 on the Lower Pannonia page, but 'installed in 864' on the Pribina page; his death is undated and the end year 876 is the March page's transfer of Lower Pannonia to Arnulf of Carinthia.

rulers.name: Braslav
rulers.title: dux of Lower Pannonia
rulers.note: 'the last dux of Lower Pannonia between at least 884 and 896', under Arnulf of Carinthia's overlordship; Arnulf handed Pannonia to him in 895 or 896.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has none). One outline for the whole life: the pages give the Zala-Balaton core and the Rába, Pécs and Ptuj limits but no changes of extent from 838 to c. 900. Zalavár itself is not in the gazetteer (modern Zala county is the reading). No infobox on the Lower Pannonia page; the Pribina page gives no area.

ledger.note: 838: The Franks install Pribina over Lower Pannonia. 'Ratimir emerged as ruler of Lower Pannonian regions around the Drava and Sava. In the same year, Frankish count Radbod deposed him, and the Franks installed Pribina' (Principality of Lower Pannonia page); the Pribina page has Louis the German send Ratpot against Ratimir in 838; the March of Pannonia page dates the establishment of the duchy to 839. Ratimir's realm has no dossier, so the counterpart is nobody.

ledger.note: 839: 'King Louis the German had the Slavic Duchy of Lower Pannonia established in 839, ruled by ... Prince Pribina with his residence at Zalavár on Lake Balaton' (March of Pannonia page). The Principality of Lower Pannonia page dates the Frankish installation of Pribina to 838 (Count Radbod deposed Ratimir) and says 'local Slavic princes governed the Principality of Lower Pannonia under Frankish suzerainty, within the March of Pannonia'; 'the polity was a vassal principality of the Frankish Empire' and 'both marches were vassals to East Francia'. The vassal tint starts in 839 to match march-of-pannonia /ledger/1; the state itself is founded in 838. The overlord is read as the March of Pannonia, the East Frankish frontier command; east-franks is the alternative. Mirror of march-of-pannonia's 839 vassal_start (reviewer finding applied).

ledger.note: c. 900: 'the Frankish Empire, which lasted until the Magyar conquest (c. 900)' (Principality of Lower Pannonia page); the March of Pannonia page says only that 'by the 890s, the Pannonian March seems to have disappeared'. Braslav ruled 884-896 'under the overlordship of Arnulf of Carinthia', who handed Pannonia to him in 895 or 896 (the same page; Arnulf received Lower Pannonia in 876, March page). The relation ends with the Magyar conquest and the principality's own end; mirror of march-of-pannonia's 900 vassal_end (reviewer finding applied).

ledger.note: c. 900: The Magyars overrun the Pannonian Basin. 'Frankish domination lasted until the Magyar conquest (c. 900)'; Arnulf had handed Pannonia to Braslav in 895 or 896 to secure the frontier against the Hungarians, who had conquered Great Moravia. The Battle of Pressburg (907) follows.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from three pages (Principality of Lower Pannonia, Pribina, March of Pannonia); the counterpart in the march-of-pannonia dossier's 839 vassal_start and 900 vassal_end events. Disagreements: the start (838 on the Lower Pannonia page, 'late 830s' on Pribina's, 839 on the March page's, 10 January 846 for the formal grant); who deposed Ratimir (Count Radbod or Ratpot); when Kocel succeeded (861 or 864). 838 is used. No infobox on the main page and no area: the outline is a reading by modern counties; the principality's real extent in 838-845 is not given. Its overlord was the March of Pannonia (a vassal tint on march-of-pannonia) and, from 876, Arnulf of Carinthia; the ledger now books the vassal_start (839, to match march-of-pannonia /ledger/1, the state itself being founded in 838) and the vassal_end (900) with counterpart march-of-pannonia, the mirror of that dossier's two events (reviewer finding, 2026-10-25); the pages also call the polity a 'vassal principality of the Frankish Empire' and say 'both marches were vassals to East Francia', so east-franks is the alternative overlord. Cliopatria has no row; Great Moravia (814-910), the Magyars (840-910) and the East Franks 850-910 shapes may overlap this land. The Wikidata id is left null. Gazetteer names needed: places Zalavár (Mosapurc), Pécs; regions Lower Pannonia, Pannonia. Not on the pages: the 884 Moravian takeover that some accounts date to 883 (the page gives no takeover date); Methodius's diocese (dates not given on the Lower Pannonia page). Repair note: the reviewer replaced Nagykanizsa (a one-cell urban county whose alt names include 'Zala megye') by Zala in all seven places, which puts Zalavár inside the shape; the Zala, Somogy, Baranya and Ptuj outline is unchanged.
